items.stem: State the rule to determine the direction of a (a) magnetic field produced around a straight conductor carrying current and (b) force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.
items.answer: (a) Maxwell's Right-Hand Thumb Rule can be used to determine the direction of magnetic field lines around a current-carrying conductor. According to the right-hand thumb rule, imagine you are holding a straight conductor in your right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of the current. The direction of curl of the fingers of the right hand then gives the direction of the magnetic field lines. (b) When a current carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field it experiences a force. The direction of this force is determined by Fleming's left-hand rule. According to this rule, if the forefinger, the middle finger and the thumb of our left hand are stretched mutually perpendicular to each other in such a way that the forefinger points along the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger points along the direction of the current, then the thumb will indicate the direction of the force acting on the conductor.

items.stem: Answer the following questions: (i) Why do we connect earth wire in a house? Give two reasons. (ii) What type of current is used in household supply? (iii) What type of current is given by a cell? (iv) To which wire do you connect fuse wire in a household circuit?
items.answer: (i) The earth wire is used: (a) to keep our electrical appliances safe from damage, and (b) to save us from electric shock due to leakage of current. (ii) AC (alternating current). (iii) DC (direct current). (iv) The live wire.

items.stem: Draw a schematic labelled diagram of a domestic wiring circuit which includes (i) a main fuse (ii) a power meter (iii) one light point (iv) a power plug
items.answer: The schematic diagram of a domestic wiring circuit is drawn as follows: the live (red) and neutral (black) wires from the pole enter the house through the main fuse, which is put in the live wire, and then pass through the electricity power meter. From the meter the supply goes to the distribution box, from which two separate parallel circuits are taken out: a 5 A circuit feeding the light point through its switch, and a 15 A circuit feeding the power plug. The power plug also carries the earth wire (green), which is connected to a metal plate buried deep in the earth.

items.stem: Write the characteristics of electricity supplied for domestic use.
items.answer: (i) The electricity supplied for domestic use is A.C. of 220 volts having a frequency of 50 Hz. (ii) Generally there are two separate circuits within the house, one with 5 A rating for bulbs, etc. and the other with 15 A for appliances with higher power ratings.

items.stem: When magnetic field lines for a bar magnet are plotted, lines are closer near the poles than in the middle of the magnet. Explain.
items.answer: The degree of closeness of the magnetic field lines depends upon the strength of the magnetic field. The magnetic field is stronger near the poles. That is why the magnetic field lines are closer near the poles than in the middle of the magnet.

items.stem: Why do we use parallel circuit arrangement for domestic wiring?
items.answer: (i) In domestic wiring each appliance gets the same (equal) potential difference. (ii) In domestic wiring each appliance has a separate switch to turn the flow of current through it on or off, so the appliances are connected in parallel to each other.

items.stem: What is the capacity of the fuse wire used in our household circuit?
items.answer: We should use a fuse wire whose capacity is slightly more than the maximum current that can flow in the circuit. A fuse of capacity 5 ampere is used in the live wire which supplies electricity to low rating appliances like a fan, bulb, etc., and a fuse of capacity 15 ampere is used in the live wire which supplies electricity to high rating appliances (having power of 1000 watt or more) like a geyser, heater, etc.
items.ocr: TWO MARKS item printed in the column that falls inside the THREE MARKS character range.

items.stem: How is a fuse wire used to avoid fire due to short circuiting?
items.answer: A fuse wire is connected in series with the live wire, so the current passes through the fuse wire before entering our household circuit. If there is short circuiting or overloading in the household circuit, a large current is drawn; the fuse wire gets heated and melts. As a result the circuit breaks and the current stops flowing, which prevents a fire.

items.stem: Answer the following questions: (i) What is the direction of magnetic field lines outside a bar magnet? (ii) The magnetic field lines in a given region are getting crowded. What does it indicate? (iii) State one advantage of AC over DC.
items.answer: (i) Outside a bar magnet the magnetic field lines are directed from the north pole to the south pole. (ii) Crowding of the field lines indicates that the strength of the magnetic field is higher in that region. (iii) AC voltage can be stepped up and transmitted over long distances without much loss of energy.
items.ocr: The printed key reads 'AC voltage can be stopped up'; corrected to 'stepped up'.

items.stem: The flow of current in a circular loop of wire creates a magnetic field at its centre. How may the existence of this field be detected? State the rule which helps to predict the direction of this magnetic field.
items.answer: Take a cardboard sheet and drill two fine holes P and Q on it along a straight line at a suitable distance. Take an insulated copper wire loop and pass it through the holes so that the loop is in a vertical plane. Connect a 6-12 V battery B and a plug key K to the ends of the wire loop. Put a sensitive compass at the centre point O of the cardboard; the compass rests in the north-south direction. Now put the plug in key K so that a current begins to flow in the loop. We observe that the compass needle gets deflected. This shows that a magnetic field is set up at the centre of the current-carrying circular loop. The direction of the field is given by the right-hand thumb rule: curl the fingers of the right hand along the direction of the current in the loop and the stretched thumb gives the direction of the magnetic field at the centre.

items.stem: A coil of insulated copper wire is connected to a galvanometer. What would happen if a bar magnet is (i) pushed into the coil? (ii) withdrawn from inside the coil? (iii) held stationary inside the coil?
items.answer: (i) Due to the change in magnetic flux linked with the coil, a current is induced and the galvanometer shows a deflection (say towards the right). (ii) Due to the change in magnetic flux linked with the coil, the galvanometer again shows a deflection, but in the opposite sense (say towards the left, opposite to that in case (i)). (iii) As the magnet is stationary there is no change in the magnetic flux linked with the coil, so no current is induced and the galvanometer shows no deflection.
items.ocr: The printed solution (i) reads 'change in magnitude flux'; corrected to 'change in magnetic flux'.

items.stem: How can the strength of the magnetic field of a solenoid be increased?
items.answer: The strength of the magnetic field of a solenoid can be increased by (i) increasing the number of turns in the solenoid, (ii) increasing the strength of the current flowing through the solenoid, and (iii) placing a soft iron core along the axis of the solenoid.

items.stem: Draw the direction of magnetic field in a circular current loop.
items.answer: If the current flows in the clockwise direction, the magnetic field enters into the plane of the loop and that face behaves like a south pole. If the current flows in the anticlockwise direction, the magnetic field comes out of the plane and that face behaves like a north pole.

items.stem: Why does a current-carrying solenoid behave as a bar magnet?
items.answer: A current-carrying solenoid behaves as a bar magnet because when current passes through the solenoid, the magnetic field produced is very much similar to that of a bar magnet. One end of the coil acts like a south pole and the other end acts like a north pole.

items.stem: An electron enters a uniform magnetic field at right angles to it as shown in the figure given below. In which direction will this electron move? State the rule applied by you in finding the direction of motion of the electron.
items.answer: The electron will move perpendicular to the plane of the paper and upwards (out of the paper). The direction of the force is perpendicular to both the direction of the magnetic field and the direction of the current, as given by Fleming's left-hand rule, remembering that the conventional current is opposite to the direction of motion of the electron.

items.stem: A student while studying the force experienced by a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field records the following observations: (i) The force experienced by the conductor increases as the current is increased. (ii) The force experienced by the conductor decreases as the strength of the magnetic field is increased. Which of the two observations is correct and why?
items.answer: Observation (i) is correct. It is so because the force experienced by a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field is directly proportional to the strength of the current. Observation (ii) is wrong, because the force is also directly proportional to the strength of the magnetic field, so it increases rather than decreases when the field is made stronger.

items.stem: Why can short circuit lead to fire in the house or building?
items.answer: When short circuiting occurs, the resistance of the circuit decreases to a very small value. Then, according to Ohm's law, the current increases enormously. This results in heating of the live wires and produces a spark at the place of the short circuit, which may cause a fire in the building.

items.stem: A current carrying straight conductor is placed in a magnetic field perpendicular to it, so that it experiences a force. How will this force get affected on: (i) doubling the magnitude of current? (ii) reversing the direction of current flow?
items.answer: (i) On doubling the magnitude of the current, the force gets doubled. (ii) On reversing the direction of the current, the direction of the force gets reversed, its magnitude remaining unchanged.

items.stem: The diagram below shows a coil connected to a centre zero galvanometer G. The galvanometer shows a deflection to the right when the N pole of a powerful magnet is moved to the right as shown. (i) Explain why the deflection occurs in the galvanometer. (ii) Does the direction of current in the coil appear clockwise or anti-clockwise when viewed from end A? (iii) State the observation in G when the coil is moved away from N. (iv) State the observation in G when both the coil and the magnet are moved to the right at the same speed.
items.answer: (i) This is due to the change in magnetic flux linked with the coil. Because of the changing magnetic flux an induced emf is produced in the coil, hence an induced current flows through the galvanometer. (ii) The current appears clockwise when viewed from end A. (iii) The galvanometer now deflects towards the left. (iv) No deflection is observed, as there is no relative motion between the magnet and the coil.

items.stem: Answer the following questions: (i) What is the direction of magnetic field lines outside a bar magnet? (ii) What is the SI unit of magnetic field? (iii) What does crowding of magnetic field lines indicate? (iv) What is the frequency of AC in India? (v) Name two organs in the human body where magnetic field is quite significant.
